acceptanceCriteria: processGroupQuiescentBy (or its caller) treats an exited, unreaped leader whose group has no other live member as quiescent on Linux (for example via the existing /proc held-group proof), so a group that obeys TERM returns before the grace expires.
A focused Linux test (CI or container) shows a TERM-obeying group with a 5 s grace stopping in well under 1 s, and a TERM-ignoring descendant still being SIGKILLed after the grace.
macOS behaviour is unchanged; the owning procgroup requirement records the rule.
body: Observed 2026-10-22 on batch PR #1534 (go-product-shard 4, job 119794317101): TestSourceViewCancellationTerminatesGitProcessGroup with a 1-minute TerminateGrace (V1-2319) took 60.01 s on Linux CI and failed its 25 s bound; on macOS it finishes in milliseconds. Reproduced in golang:1.27.2 Docker: with a 5 s grace the test takes exactly 5.14 s although the shell exits on TERM at once. Cause (inferred from internal/procgroup/process_posix.go cleanupProcessGroupBeforeReap -> processGroupQuiescentBy): the group probe is kill(-pgid, 0), and Linux keeps succeeding while the exited leader is held unreaped as a zombie, so the group never reads quiet until the grace deadline. Production uses the 100 ms default grace, so the cost is 100 ms per cancelled/timed-out child, but any caller with a longer grace pays it in full and the quiescence signal is wrong. The batch fixed only the test (grace lowered to 5 s, commit 3ab77c0b9).
title: procgroup: on Linux every signalled group waits out the full TERM grace because the unreaped leader keeps signal 0 succeeding
